Below is a taxonomy built only from the rules you provided. I group the puzzles by the main object the solver constructs and by the dominant constraint style.

# Taxonomy of the listed grid-based logic games

## I. Cell-state placement puzzles
These puzzles primarily ask the solver to decide the state of each cell: black/white, bulb/no bulb, symbol choice, number choice, etc.

### I.A. Binary shading / painting puzzles
Cells are mainly classified as black vs white, painted vs unpainted.

#### I.A.1. Shading with adjacency and connectivity constraints
- **Heyawake**  
  Paint cells; black cells cannot touch orthogonally; white cells must stay connected; room counts and “no straight white through more than two rooms”.
- **Hitori**  
  Black out repeated numbers; black cells cannot touch orthogonally; white cells must form one connected network.
- **Kurodoko**  
  Shade black cells; numbered cells stay white; black cells cannot touch orthogonally; white cells connected; numbers count visible white cells.
- **Nurikabe**  
  Fill cells black/white; numbered cells stay white; white regions have one number and specified size; black cells form one connected wall; no 2×2 black.
- **Usowan**  
  Shade cells; numbered cells stay white; black cells cannot touch orthogonally; white cells connected; one wrong clue per room.
- **Yajilin**  
  Shade some cells black while also drawing a loop; black cells cannot touch orthogonally; clue cells are excluded from loop and shading.

#### I.A.2. Shading with local shape restrictions on black and/or white regions
- **Choco Banana**  
  Black connected cells must form rectangles/squares; white connected cells must not form rectangles/squares; numbers give area size.
- **Nurimisaki**  
  White cells connected; both black and white forbidden from forming 2×2 or larger square blocks; circled cells must be “promontories”.
- **Nurimeizu**  
  Whole rooms are black or white; white cells must form a maze from S to G; white may not form a loop; neither color may form 2×2 or larger squares.
- **Shakashaka**  
  Place triangular black pieces in cells so remaining white parts form rectangles/squares.
- **Tilepaint**  
  Color whole tiles black or white; clues count black cells in directions; final picture forms an outline.
- **Sto-stone**  
  Fill colored cells black under room constraints; black cells cannot connect across room borders before “dropping”; after dropping they fill bottom half.

#### I.A.3. Shading with region-pair or block-balance conditions
- **Norinori**  
  Black cells occur only in domino-like pairs; each room contains exactly two black cells.
- **Nuritwin**  
  Each region contains exactly two shaded blocks of equal size; shaded cells globally connected; same-region twin blocks cannot touch; no 2×2 all shaded.

### I.B. Light-placement puzzles
- **Akari**  
  Place bulbs in white cells; numbered black cells count adjacent bulbs; bulbs illuminate orthogonally; all white cells illuminated; bulbs cannot see each other.

### I.C. Symbol-placement puzzles
Cells receive one of a small set of symbols rather than just black/white.

- **Juosan**  
  Fill every cell with either — or |; territory clues compare counts of the two symbols; run-length restrictions differ by symbol orientation.
- **Shakashaka**  
  Also fits here because cells receive one of four triangle orientations or remain empty/white.
- **Evolomino**  
  Place square marks in some cells; connected marked cells form blocks with arrow-based growth rules.

### I.D. Number-placement puzzles
The main task is to place numbers in cells.

#### I.D.1. Latin / room-completion style
- **Sudoku**  
  Fill 1–9 so each row, column, and 3×3 box contains all digits.
- **Makaro**  
  Each room contains 1 up to room size; arrow clues indicate local maximum direction; equal numbers cannot touch across rooms.
- **Ripple Effect**  
  Each room contains consecutive numbers from 1; equal numbers in row/column must be spaced at least their value apart.

#### I.D.2. Region-size labeling
- **Fillomino**  
  Partition into same-number polyominoes whose size equals the number; equal-sized regions cannot touch orthogonally.

#### I.D.3. Path/sequence number placement
- **Hebi**  
  Place 1–5 snake segments in white cells; each snake is sequential; snakes cannot touch; directional visibility restrictions from snake heads; arrowed black clues indicate nearest seen segment.
- **Nansuke**  
  Fill blanks with digits from a given list; entries run horizontally or vertically.

---

## II. Region-division puzzles
These puzzles primarily ask the solver to partition the grid into regions or blocks.

### II.A. Partition into arbitrary or constrained polyominoes
- **Five Cells**  
  Divide grid into regions of exactly five cells; clues count bordering lines around a cell.
- **Sashigane**  
  Divide into one-cell-wide L-shaped regions; circles mark bends and may give size; arrows mark ends pointing toward bend.
- **Shikaku**  
  Divide into rectangles; each rectangle contains one clue equal to its area.
- **Double Choco**  
  Draw borders to divide into blocks; each block contains matching white and gray shapes; clues give half-block size by color.

### II.B. Partition implied by filled cells / blocks
- **Chained Block**  
  Fill cells black/white; connected black cells form blocks with size clues or ?; every block has one clue; corner-touching blocks form chains with no repeated size-and-shape in a chain.
- **Fillomino**  
  Also belongs here because the number filling induces a partition into polyominoes.
- **LITS**  
  Each room contains one tetromino; tetrominoes across rooms must connect globally and obey non-touching same-shape rule.
- **Nuritwin**  
  Each outlined region contains two shaded blocks of equal size.

---

## III. Loop-drawing puzzles
These puzzles ask for a single closed loop, usually through cell centers or along grid edges.

### III.A. Cell-center loop puzzles
The loop passes through cells.

#### III.A.1. Pure loop with clue cells controlling local behavior
- **Masyu**  
  Single loop through all circles; white circles force straight passage with a turn adjacent; black circles force a turn with straight continuation on both sides.
- **Mid-loop**  
  Single loop through all black circles; each black circle is the midpoint of a straight segment.
- **Nagareru**  
  Single directed loop through arrow cells; wind from black arrows constrains movement direction and forced bending.
- **Moon-or-Sun**  
  Single loop; each room entered once; in each room loop uses all moons or all suns, alternating type between consecutive rooms.
- **Suraromu**  
  Single loop through all gates exactly once each; start/end at open circle; numbered gates specify crossing order.
- **Yajilin**  
  Single loop through non-black, non-clue cells, combined with black-cell placement.

#### III.A.2. Loop with room-based turning/straight conditions
- **Dotchi-Loop**  
  Single loop through white-circle cells; in each bold region, all white circles are either all straight or all turning; black-circle cells are forbidden.

### III.B. Edge/dot loop puzzles
The loop is drawn on grid lines between dots.

- **Slitherlink**  
  Single loop on edges; clues count incident edges around cells.

---

## IV. Path-connection puzzles without a single loop
These puzzles draw one or more paths, but not necessarily one closed loop.

### IV.A. Pair-connection paths
- **Numberlink**  
  Connect equal numbers with non-crossing, non-branching paths through cells.

### IV.B. Directed or length-constrained path assignment
- **Pencils**  
  Mark straight pencil bodies and draw a line from each tip; pencil numbers give pencil length and line length; lines may turn but not cross themselves or branch.
- **Satogaeri**  
  Move circles orthogonally so each country ends with one circle; numbered circles move exactly that many cells; paths cannot cross or pass over circles.
- **Yosenabe**  
  Move circles by straight arrows into gray areas; arrows do not bend or cross; gray-area numbers equal sum of entering circles.

### IV.C. Maze / route existence under shading
- **Nurimeizu**  
  Create a white-cell maze from S to G with shortest-path conditions involving circles and triangles.

---

## V. Object-linking / network construction puzzles
These puzzles build a connected network rather than a loop or region partition.

### V.A. Bridge/network puzzles
- **Hashiwokakero**  
  Connect numbered islands with 0–2 bridges per pair; bridges cannot cross; all islands become one connected network.

---

## VI. Movement / relocation puzzles
The main action is moving tokens or circles to valid destinations.

- **Satogaeri**  
  Move circles so each country has one circle; movement length may be fixed by clue.
- **Yosenabe**  
  Move circles into gray areas by straight arrows; area sums matter.

(These also fit under path-connection, but movement is the dominant framing in the rules.)

---

## VII. Shape-construction and growth puzzles
The solver builds explicit geometric shapes or evolving polyominoes.

- **Evolomino**  
  Place squares so each connected block contains exactly one square on a pre-drawn arrow; later blocks along an arrow grow by one square without rotation or reflection.
- **LITS**  
  Place tetrominoes, one per room, with connectivity and shape-adjacency restrictions.
- **Sashigane**  
  Construct L-shaped regions.
- **Shikaku**  
  Construct rectangles.
- **Choco Banana**  
  Black connected components must be rectangles/squares.
- **Shakashaka**  
  White residual areas must be rectangles/squares.

---

# Cross-cutting taxonomy by primary constraint type

Some puzzles fit multiple families. Using only the rules, these are the main recurring constraint styles:

## A. Connectivity constraints
Require one connected set or forbid disconnection.
- **Akari**: all white cells illuminated
- **Hashiwokakero**: all islands connected
- **Heyawake**: white connected
- **Hitori**: white connected
- **Kurodoko**: white connected
- **LITS**: shaded cells connected
- **Nurikabe**: black connected wall
- **Nurimisaki**: white connected
- **Nuritwin**: shaded cells connected
- **Usowan**: white connected

## B. Non-touching constraints
Forbid orthogonal contact of certain objects.
- **Akari**: bulbs cannot illuminate each other
- **Hebi**: snakes cannot touch
- **Heyawake**: black cells cannot touch
- **Hitori**: black cells cannot touch
- **Kurodoko**: black cells cannot touch
- **LITS**: same tetromino shape cannot touch edgewise across rooms
- **Nurikabe / Nurimisaki / Nuritwin**: no 2×2 all-black/shaded or similar square restrictions
- **Usowan**: colored cells cannot touch
- **Yajilin**: black cells cannot touch

## C. Region-size constraints
Numbers specify area/block size.
- **Chained Block**
- **Choco Banana**
- **Double Choco**
- **Fillomino**
- **Makaro** (room contains 1..size)
- **Nurikabe**
- **Nuritwin**
- **Sashigane**
- **Shikaku**

## D. Visibility / line-of-sight constraints
Clues count or restrict what is seen in straight lines.
- **Akari**
- **Hebi**
- **Kurodoko**
- **Kurotto**
- **Tilepaint**
- **Yajilin** (counts black cells in arrow direction)

## E. Loop-local behavior constraints
Clues determine whether the loop turns or goes straight.
- **Dotchi-Loop**
- **Masyu**
- **Mid-loop**
- **Moon-or-Sun**
- **Nagareru**
- **Suraromu**

## F. Room-based constraints
Bold-bordered regions impose local rules.
- **Dotchi-Loop**
- **Double Choco**
- **Five Cells**
- **Heyawake**
- **Juosan**
- **LITS**
- **Makaro**
- **Moon-or-Sun**
- **Nurimeizu**
- **Nuritwin**
- **Ripple Effect**
- **Sto-stone**
- **Tilepaint**
- **Usowan**
- **Satogaeri** (“Countries”)

## G. Shape-identity / congruence constraints
Shapes must match, differ, or evolve.
- **Chained Block**: no repeated size-and-shape in a chain, including rotations/reflections
- **Double Choco**: white and gray areas in a block have same shape up to rotation/reflection
- **Evolomino**: successive blocks grow by one square without rotation/flipping
- **LITS**: same tetromino shape variants cannot touch
- **Nuritwin**: two equal-sized shaded blocks per region

# Highest-level summary

Using only the provided rules, these games fall into six major structural types:

1. **Cell filling / marking**  
   Decide what goes in each cell: black/white, bulb, symbol, number, triangle, square.  
   Examples: **Akari, Heyawake, Hitori, Kurodoko, Sudoku, Fillomino**.

2. **Region partitioning**  
   Draw borders or otherwise divide the grid into blocks of constrained size/shape.  
   Examples: **Five Cells, Sashigane, Shikaku, Double Choco**.

3. **Loop construction**  
   Draw one closed loop, either through cells or along edges.  
   Examples: **Masyu, Slitherlink, Dotchi-Loop, Mid-loop, Moon-or-Sun**.

4. **Path / connection construction**  
   Draw non-loop paths connecting endpoints or representing motion.  
   Examples: **Numberlink, Pencils, Satogaeri, Yosenabe**.

5. **Network construction**  
   Build a connected graph-like structure.  
   Example: **Hashiwokakero**.

6. **Hybrid puzzles**  
   Combine two structures at once, such as loop + shading or maze + room coloring.  
   Examples: **Yajilin, Nurimeizu, Sto-stone**.
